audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill for rows 0-4 while the content layer read Karma/Karma/Karma/Karma/Vladimir, and content win[5] gave the First-item row back to Karma while the full layer gave it to Vladimir. Two layers, two answers.
audit.why: Karma genuinely owns levels 1-5: Inner Flame reaches 950 against Transfusion's 600, and Vladimir pays his own health for Tides of Blood. He takes over at 6 and does not give it back — Crimson Pact converts AP into health, so the poke war he was losing stops mattering once he has an item.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 to Karma, rows 4-6 to Vladimir, in both layers, with every why rewritten to match. This also resolves packet.defects' complaint that the chart handed Karma 5 of 7 stages in a matchup she wins 47.2%.
sources: enemyKit Q range 600, E cost = own health, P Crimson Pact

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes claimed Karma's first item restores the poke war and lets her 'threaten his HP bar directly again'.
audit.why: Crimson Pact gives 1.6 health per point of AP, so every item he buys widens the bar your chip has to move. His first item is his spike, not yours.
audit.corrected: spikes[2], mid and whys[5] rewritten on Crimson Pact; Hemoplague's flat 120s and Sanguine Pool's 28s rank-1 cooldown added to the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two decisive interactions were absent: Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetability eating a Mantra commit, and Vladimir's Transfusion/Hemoplague sustain needing Grievous Wounds. breakdown.cooldowns contained no number (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 down to 16s maxed and grants 2 seconds untargetable, so a Mantra-Q fired into it is spent on empty ground. Transfusion is 0 mana on a 4.6s cooldown maxed and heals him; Hemoplague heals him per champion hit. Anti-heal timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries all three numbers; tradeBad, dos/donts and wants.you[2] state the pool-bait and the Grievous Wounds requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading rules were the generic Karma template with no reference to this enemy.
audit.why: The trade rule here is entirely gated on Sanguine Pool's cooldown.
audit.corrected: tradeGood/tradeBad/breakdown.trading now key the commit to Sanguine Pool being down.
